experiment.question: What does a 14,000-device deployment do over a 7.5 hour soak, including provisiond's rolling rescans?
experiment.plan: Retroactive capture of 2026-09-02T22:00:00Z to 2026-09-03T05:32:19Z, the period after the 20:02:30Z OpenNMS restart, fleet held at 14,000 devices with no injected latency. capture.py start/stop was NOT used: it defines its window from the workstation clock and cannot target a past one. Prometheus series were dumped with this skill's own prom.dump_all() over explicit bounds; sysstat, inventory and journalctl were recovered from host history. Live collectors are recorded as disabled, not failed.

sut.config_delta: collectd-configuration.xml: threads 50 -> 100. Kafka exclusive forwarding (forward.metrics=true, metricTopic=metrics, EmptyResourceStorageDao, no local time-series store). Thresholding disabled. Database connection pool 50 -> 250. JAVA_HEAP_SIZE 10240, so -Xms8192m -Xmx10240m on OpenJDK 21.0.12 with G1GC. Provisiond entirely at stock: scan pool corePoolSize 10, maxPoolSize Integer.MAX_VALUE. OpenNMS restarted 2026-09-02T20:02:30Z. GC logging was NOT configured on either JVM and was enabled at runtime with jcmd VM.log during this capture; the gc.log files under hosts/*/jvm/*/ were pulled by hand because the skill derives GC log paths from the JVM command line. NOT IN GIT: the heap raise, the netsim resize to 4 vCPU / 8 GiB and nl6 v0.28.0 are live-only.

host.cpu: Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU E5-2650 v4 @ 2.20GHz, 8 cores

workload.generator_scenario: nl6 cisco_crs_x.json, 14,000 devices, 144 interfaces each, SNMP v2c, 10.42.0.0/16 octets 0-55
